[2026-10-08] c:6056591110 comment by maflcko (member):
The Windows CI fails, as usual. It fails after 1s: `interface_http.py failed (exit code 1), Duration: 1 s`, so it seems unrelated to timeouts...
[2026-10-08] c:6058672293 comment by maflcko (member):
Hmm, I guess with a timeout the socket can go through `select()` and then manifest this race. Still, the test seems like it should be fixed and only assert the essential outcome: 413 logged and socket closed. I'll push a commit for that ...
[2026-10-08] c:6061354469 comment by maflcko (member):
Heh, looks like this accidentally fixes https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/issues/368.

At least according to @pinheadmz's Fable, IIUC: https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/issues/368#issuecomment-6059544560
[2026-10-08] r:5463370919 review APPROVED by pinheadmz (member):
ACK fa5551cc6de1629ef800d8b1f7697af923a953bb

Built and tested on macos/arm64 as well as NetBSD VM in qemu, I know its not OpenBSD but its what i had lying around. Also ran the intermittent test on a loop in an OpenBSD ci: https://github.com/pinheadmz/bitcoin/actions/runs/37847855161

Reviewed the changes, came to the same conclusion that the connection needed a timeout set before the first `connect()`. I'm a little nervous that without a catch / retry we'll end up with a flaky test again but then we might have more data to diagnose with.

Change to the excessive size test makes sense as well - using the server log to assert something happened is more reliable than waiting for an event on the client side to tell us what happened.
